scope: Crosswalk from selected 1864 India Office transfer/version families to modern MSS EUR HODGSON volume locations, with 1921 dimension-based rebinding treated as an explicit collection-level dispersion mechanism.
central_claim: Version families co-custodied in 1864 are now dispersed across modern volumes; the Cambridge catalogue states that 1921 arrangement partly grouped documents by physical dimensions and could separate originals from translations simply because their paper sizes differed.

collection_history.deposit: Hodgson papers deposited in India Office Library in 1864
collection_history.historical_numbering_note: numbering runs to 108 because 13 scrolls were present in sequence
collection_history.binding_rule: partly by physical dimensions, grouping items of similar size
collection_history.documented_effect: items belonging together, including original manuscripts and translations, were sometimes bound in different places because written on different sizes of paper
collection_history.count_state_warning: Historical and current extent counts differ and must remain unreconciled until cataloguing history is reconstructed.

source_control_rules: The collection-level 1921 dimension rule is explicit; do not claim that size caused a specific item's separation without binding-level evidence.
Same 1864 large bundle does not mean same immediate wrapper or sheet adjacency.
Modern direct cross-references vary in strength; preserve original/translation/copy wording separately from broad similarity links.

Modern volume count is not equivalent to 1864 transfer-unit count.
